policy.title: Benchmark evidence policy
policy.summary: Benchmarks are supporting evidence, not our final ranking. We identify the exact model/version, source, snapshot date and harness. Product scores are not treated as model scores, and results from different harness versions are not compared directly.

sources.name: Arena Text Leaderboard
sources.measures: Human preference in anonymous model-vs-model battles across open-ended text tasks.
sources.caveat: A product such as ChatGPT or Claude can change its default model; Arena ranks specific model versions, not the whole product. Checked 2026-09-14 and re-checked 2026-09-21, 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05: the text leaderboard served snapshot id "latest" dated 2026-10-02 (vote cutoff 2026-10-02T11:00:00.000Z, 8,626,731 votes, 413 models), read through the canonical text-overall-style_control route, the alternate text-overall route and the embedded data payload, all agreeing. Every tracked row was re-read from that snapshot. All six keep the same exact model version as before; every rank moved down 2-4 places (57/59/68/82/85/113 became 60/62/70/86/89/115). Five of the six ratings were unchanged to the board's rounding and one moved by a single point, against confidence intervals of +/-2 to +/-6, so this is leaderboard drift rather than a change in product quality. Vote counts for five of the six tracked listings fell slightly even as the board-wide total rose, which is consistent with the snapshot being recomputed rather than only appended to. Two newer same-board listings were again seen and deliberately NOT added as rows: grok-4.5-text (rank 50 in this snapshot, 1466 +/-4 band) and deepseek-v4-pro-high-20260813 (rank 56 in this snapshot, 1464 +/-7 band). This registry carries one representative exact listing per product family, and the site's generators key rows by tool_slug, so a second row for the same family would silently overwrite the first in every generated comparison rather than adding evidence.

sources.name: Arena-Rank methodology
sources.measures: Bradley-Terry ratings with reweighting and confidence intervals from pairwise preference data.
sources.use_for: Explaining how Arena scores are produced
sources.caveat: Human preference can reward style and verbosity; it is not an objective factuality test.

sources.name: SWE-bench Verified
sources.measures: Percentage of 500 human-validated real GitHub issues resolved by a coding model or agent.
sources.caveat: Scores depend heavily on the agent harness. mini-SWE-agent v1.x and v2.x results are not directly comparable. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05: the site still publishes a machine-readable results payload (an embedded leaderboard-data JSON block covering Multilingual, Test, Verified, Lite and Multimodal). The Verified group is unchanged at 180 rows dated 2023-10-10 to 2026-02-26; the newest is still a mini-SWE-agent run on Gemini 3 Pro at 69.6% resolved, and the highest score in the group is Sonar Foundation Agent at 79.2% (2025-12-05). No Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Replit, or other tracked end-user product appears in that Verified set, so no product-level coding row is added from it. The page text still confirms the 500-instance human-validated subset.

sources.name: LiveBench
sources.measures: Objective, frequently refreshed tasks across reasoning, math, coding, language, instruction following and data analysis.
sources.caveat: Always state the release; questions and model configurations change between snapshots. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05: the repository is live and active (latest commit seen 2026-09-29), but its public changelog still ends at 2026-01-08 and the README still shows "Top models as of 30th September 2024". A dated leaderboard can be read without a browser through the app's client-side data route: the app's release list still ends at 2026-06-25 and serves table_2026_06_25.csv, which now holds 66 model rows across 23 tasks in 7 categories (an earlier check recorded 58, then 63). The file's own Last-Modified header is 2026-09-29, so the publisher is still editing the June-dated table without publishing a newer release; treat the row count as a moving target and the release date as the fixed fact. Newer model configs keep appearing in the repository (gpt-6-sol-max, gpt-6-luna-max, claude-sonnet-5-5, gpt-6.1-sol) without a matching published table, so treat LiveBench as release-pinned evidence, not a current ranking.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis methodology
sources.measures: Independent intelligence, latency, speed, price, speech, image and video model evaluations.
sources.use_for: Cost/speed context and non-text modality methodology
sources.caveat: API model measurements do not equal the complete end-user product experience. Re-checked 2026-10-05: the methodology page is live and still serves no dated per-model score table, so no Artificial Analysis row exists in this registry.

sources.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1 leaderboard (frozen; subdomain now serves 4.0)
sources.measures: Accuracy of an agent + model + reasoning-effort configuration on 89 complex containerized terminal tasks.
sources.use_for: Coding agents and terminal-capable development tools
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-28 and re-checked 2026-10-05: https://www.tbench.ai/leaderboard/terminal-bench/2.1 still returns a 308 redirect to https://www.tbench.ai/?version=2.1, and every route on that host - including ?version=2.1 - serves the Terminal-Bench 4.0 board (title "Terminal-Bench 4.0", leaderboard slug "4-0-0", board updated_at 2026-09-21T21:28:10Z, 27 rows at 330 trials each). No 2.1 rows could be read from this URL on any date, and no archived 2.1 board exists on the site. The 4.0 board lists only Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build and mini-SWE-agent configurations and carries no Cursor, Copilot or other tracked-product entry. Never present this as a model-only score; keep agent, exact model, effort, trial count and integrity metadata visible.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Image methodology
sources.measures: Blind pairwise image preference with exact model/version and matched prompt conditions.
sources.caveat: Keep text-to-image and editing pools separate; old model versions are historical evidence only. Re-checked 2026-10-05: the page is live with separate text-to-image and editing sections and still serves no dated score table.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Video methodology
sources.measures: Modality-separated video quality, latency and price comparisons.
sources.caveat: Do not compare Elo across different video modalities or output settings. Re-checked 2026-10-05: the methodology page is live and states that each modality has its own Elo pool in the Video Arena, so silent and audio-enabled outputs are not compared directly and editing is not compared with generation. No dated score table is served.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis TTS methodology
sources.measures: Provider-voice and controlled-voice human-preference comparisons for text-to-speech.
sources.caveat: Controlled-voice and provider-voice arenas answer different questions and must remain separate. Re-checked 2026-10-05: the canonical page is live at https://artificialanalysis.ai/text-to-speech/methodology (the older /text-to-speech/methodology path reached through the site's own navigation) and it separates the provider-voice and controlled-voice sections. No dated score table is served.

sources.name: Terminal-Bench: Cursor CLI + Grok 4.5 submission
sources.measures: Maintainer-verified Terminal-Bench 2.1 submission record for one exact Cursor CLI configuration.
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21, re-hashed 2026-09-28 and re-hashed 2026-10-05 against the raw submission file (sha256 a73454861c91299b501637e6df6082f2f16cf9c9f6c98f07bce315189f82eb23, 29,033 bytes, byte-identical on every check): Cursor CLI 2026.07.08-0c04a8a + cursor/grok-4.5 at high effort, 79.33% +/- 1.46, 445 trials, 8.99% reward-hack disqualifications, dated 2026-07-09. Two limits sit on it: the Terminal-Bench 2.1 README states "Community submissions are currently closed for Terminal-Bench 2.1", so the 2.1 board is frozen, and the live 4.0 board carries no Cursor entry, so there is no current Cursor reading to compare it to. Scores from 2.1 and 4.0 are different harness versions and must never be compared with each other.

sources.name: Harbor Hub — Terminal-Bench 2.1 dataset
sources.measures: The live dataset record for Terminal-Bench 2.1: which tasks the frozen board ran and which version is published.
sources.use_for: Confirming the task set behind a Terminal-Bench 2.1 configuration score
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21, 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05: the dataset page describes "Version 2.1 of Terminal-Bench", and the Terminal-Bench 2.1 repository independently holds 89 task directories (91 entries minus the README and dataset.toml files), matching the 89 tasks this page reports. Terminal-Bench 4.0 is not a "larger" task set: the current Terminal-Bench repository holds 66 task directories at its v4.0.0 release tag (published 2026-08-26). 2.1 and 4.0 are different task sets, not a small/large pair. The Hub's latest published revision is still 2.0.2 (revision 6), above 2.0.1 and 2.0.0. This page publishes the task list, not leaderboard scores; it cannot upgrade a 2.1 score into a 4.0 score.

All six tracked listings were re-read from it and all six keep the same exact model version as before. Every rank moved down 2-4 places. Five of the six ratings were unchanged to the board's rounding and one (Mistral) moved by a single point, against confidence intervals of +/-2 to +/-6, so this is leaderboard drift rather than evidence that any product got worse. Vote counts for five of the six tracked listings fell slightly (by 12-86) even as the board-wide total rose by ~98,000, which is consistent with the snapshot being recomputed rather than only appended to; the change table reports those deltas as they were measured.
